# Write social and community marketing

Produce ready-to-post work that fits the community, actor, and audience. Verify current platform rules
and format limits when they affect the result.

## Establish channel fit

Determine:

- actor: founder, company, employee, customer, or community participant;
- audience and community purpose;
- useful idea, product change, evidence, or question;
- affiliation and disclosure requirements;
- native format and realistic CTA;
- strongest skeptical response.

Recommend not posting when the community-product fit is weak. Never manufacture engagement, votes,
controversy, vulnerability, authority, or customer advocacy.

State affiliation, sponsorship, gifted access, employment, and material relationships where the
actor or channel requires disclosure. Treat UGC and customer voice as real only with provenance and
consent; otherwise label the scenario or use the operator's own voice.

## Apply the channel

### Product Hunt

Classify the product with a concrete, differentiated tagline. Explain the problem, mechanism, why now,
and invitation for feedback. Make gallery assets tell a progressive product story. Prepare honest
answers on audience, alternatives, pricing, privacy, and roadmap. Measure qualified activation and
objections, not rank alone.

### Reddit

Check the specific community's current rules and norms. Lead with a useful observation, artifact,
result, or honest question. State affiliation plainly. Make the post valuable without the click.
Prefer one well-matched community over cross-posting the same pitch.

### X

Put the claim, observation, or product change in the opening line. Compress wording, not meaning. Use
a thread only when sequence creates cumulative value. Make media carry evidence. Write replies that
advance the idea rather than repeat it.

### LinkedIn

Open on a concrete professional tension, result, or lesson. Prefer lived specificity and real
tradeoffs over inspiration. Keep line breaks readable without theatrical fragmentation. Use founder
voice for conviction and learning; company voice for product truth and proof.

## Route elsewhere

`social` produces channel-native social and community posts only. Include it when the deliverable
is a post, listing, thread, reply bank, or launch sequence an account publishes itself. Hand off when
the surface is paid, on-site, or one-to-one:

- Paid ad copy for Meta, Google, or LinkedIn → `ads`.
- Landing-page copy, headlines, taglines, on-site sections → `copy`.
- Outreach DMs and one-to-one sequences → `outreach`.
- Full video briefs with shot lists and audio plans → `video`; this command owns only the
  caption layer.

## Deliver

Return the final native post or listing first. Include only the useful supporting pieces:

- alternate hook or title when it tests a genuinely different angle;
- honest disclosure line;
- media or gallery brief;
- reply bank for likely questions and objections;
- sequence timing when multiple posts have distinct roles;
- measurement and a decision date.

Record supplied task-local limits and preview truncation checks before handoff; keep missing
checks explicit. Preserve the intended hook, disclosure,
proof, links, media role, and CTA in the visible surface; never silently truncate or cross-post the
same body into incompatible formats.

Score native posts with the five-dimension rubric in [rubric](references/rubric.md). Pass is ≥35/50
subject to the rubric hard-failure and concerns rules. Run its Discrimination Test every cycle
and score the weak comparison honestly; do not force a target score. Launch listings also load
[launch copywriter](agents/launch-copywriter-agent.md)
and [guard checker](agents/guard-checker-agent.md).

Before delivery, load the recovered method instead of paraphrasing it:

- [method](references/method.md), the
  [copywriter](agents/copywriter-agent.md), [format checker](agents/format-checker-agent.md), and
  [critic](agents/critic-agent.md);
- the matching [platform intelligence](../video/references/platform-intelligence/) pack, plus

- worked example: [social walkthrough](references/examples/social-walkthrough.md) or

If the host cannot run those as separate agents, use [sequential fallback](fallbacks/sequential.md).
One platform per artifact.

Keep publishing and account actions behind explicit approval. If the host cannot guarantee that
boundary, stop with the ready-to-post package.

## Stops

Fail closed and say which stop fired:

- **Missing input:** no actor, audience, or useful idea → stop before drafting; do not invent a
  product story.
- **Factual uncertainty:** a product claim lacks supplied proof → mark it unverified or cut it;
  never fabricate customer voice, metrics, or consent.
- **Unverified first-person:** “I live in…”, “I didn’t want…”, or other lived-experience claims
  without a verified operator-experience packet. Label the copy **proposed voice** in supporting
  notes, or write in disclosed operator affiliation without inventing a personal story.
- **Internal jargon in native copy:** NO-GO, sitting, ZIP vs npm, four-module ledger language, or
  ticket IDs. Customer wording may say the product is **not publicly released**. Keep bureaucracy in
  internal notes. Send/publish gates belong in operator notes. Do not open with a population claim
  that has no sample.
- **Credential stop:** no authenticated account exists for the target platform → deliver the
  ready-to-post package only; do not simulate access, posting, or engagement.
- **External action:** publishing, voting, replying as the actor, and account actions stay behind
  explicit human approval at action time.
- **Critic failure:** FORMAT_FAIL, a critic score below pass, or SKILL Unverified first-person /
  Internal jargon triggered on the native body → return the failure honestly; never polish or
  ship a failed draft as ready.
- **Human verdict:** readiness is advisory; a human decides whether and where to post.
